artifact: SWE-ContextBench stage 0 analysis and gate verdict

verdict.primary_statistic: packed recall@5 of the official Relationship parent, 357 distinct targets, ANY-PARENT, whole 1,007-row pool as one haystack
verdict.consequence: Stage 1 proceeds. Retrieval is not the reason to cancel anything.

like_for_like_vs_published_table_5.metric: Overall Matched (%) -- a task counts once if the gold parent appears anywhere in the top-k. Verified to be a union rather than a sum: Mem0's per-rank cells 25.25+15.15+9.09 = 49.49 exceed its Overall 39.39, so Overall is ANY-PARENT recall@k, the same statistic reported here.
like_for_like_vs_published_table_5.configuration: 99 Lite targets against the 300-row Lite experience pool -- the published configuration, reproduced exactly

rows.memphant_at_same_k: not measured at k=15; 79.80 at k=10 and 87.88 at k=25 bracket it

like_for_like_vs_published_table_5.verdict: MemPhant leads every published method at matched or SMALLER k.
caveats_that_must_travel_with_this_table: n=99. A 10pp gap is ten instances. This is a ranking, not a measurement, by this programme's own n_d >= 6 floor.
These are the benchmark authors' own runs of other people's systems. No per-instance results are published for any arm, so nothing can be paired and NO significance test is possible.
Supermemory's k=15 is not reproduced here; its row is bracketed, not matched.
The exact retrieval-unit definition each vendor used is not published. 'Matched' is assumed to mean the gold parent instance, which is the only reading consistent with the arithmetic above.
One gold parent (scikit-learn__scikit-learn-26323) is outside the 300-row Lite pool and is recorded UNREACHABLE here. It is unknown whether the published numbers account for it.

stage_2_power.ceiling_source: Table 3, Claude Sonnet 4.5 / Claude Code on Related: no-memory 19.68 -> oracle-summary 23.40
stage_2_power.expected_effect_derivation: packed recall@5 (0.7591) x ceiling (3.72pp). UPPER bound: assumes a retrieved parent helps exactly as much as an oracle-supplied one.
stage_2_power.verdict: The expected effect (2.82pp) is BELOW the MDE at every psi, including 0.05. At a realistic psi of 0.15-0.30 the power to detect it is 0.14-0.24. The instrument cannot resolve the effect it measures on the Resolved endpoint at its maximum available n -- a conclusion that applies equally to Table 4's own ranking and to Supermemory's 4.04pp margin at n=99.
stage_2_power.recommendation: CANCEL stage 2 as scoped, independently of s4-controls. If a paid run is still wanted, promote FAIL_TO_PASS to primary (Table 4 moves it 19.64 -> 55.95 versus Resolved's 26.26 -> 30.30) -- roughly ten times the effect, measured per test rather than per task.

evidence_contract.claim: MemPhant retrieves the official SWE-ContextBench Relationship parent for 75.91% of 357 targets at packed rank<=5 against the whole 1,007-row experience pool, clearing the preregistered GREEN band of 0.50; and the instrument's own published ceiling of 3.72pp sits below its minimum detectable effect at its maximum available n of 357.

harness.scorer: memphant recall mode=fast, gold-parent id match at packed rank and at trace fused_rank

corpus.note: sha256 is SWEContextBench_Experience.parquet, the ingested pool, re-verified on disk at run time against benchmarks/manifests/swe_contextbench.lock.json. 1,100 rows deduplicate to 1,007 distinct byte-identical-grouped instances.

evidence_contract.mechanism_evidence: Retrieval fired and is proven from the run's own scratch DB, not from a self-report: 1,007/1,007 experiences carry a compiled memory_unit, 1,053 embeddings exist, the worker completed 1,007 jobs and the queue was asserted empty (pending=0, dead=0) on the BENCH superuser credential, all 376 recalls returned degraded=false, and all 376 traces were fetched and carry ~550 ranked candidates each. The single-haystack construction is the mechanism under test: one subject and one scope for all 1,007 experiences, so recall ranks over the whole corpus rather than over a pool of one as the retained n=12 rehearsal did.

leakage.unit_definition: One memory unit is one experience task rendered as identity + repository + base commit + observed-at + problem_statement + hints_text. The gold merged patch is DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED.
leakage.note: Measured, not assumed. Parent problem_statement+hints contains an exact target added line (>20 chars) on 9.0% of 376 edges with mean coverage 0.0306, against a 6.9% floor produced by the TARGET's own problem statement quoting its own patch. The rejected with-patch pool measured 37.2% / 0.2856 against a same-repo random control of 9.1% / 0.0013, and was ruled inadmissible before any cell existed.
leakage.floor_kind_note: exhaustive: all 376 relationship edges were checked, not sampled.
leakage.provenance_class_note: human_published: every memory unit is upstream GitHub issue/PR prose written by third-party contributors years before this lane existed. It is emphatically NOT authored_from_target -- the with-patch variant, which WOULD have approached that class at 37.2% exact-added-line overlap, was rejected before any cell existed.

instrument_verification.license_evidence: HuggingFace record metadata at the pinned revision declares cardData.license=mit and the card README.md is pinned by sha256. NO LICENSE FILE EXISTS in either the dataset or the code repo -- independently re-confirmed. Local measurement and citation only; NOT redistribution-clear.
instrument_verification.note: The paper states 1,100 base and 376 related tasks. Measured distinct counts are 1,007 and 357. The 357 figure is corroborated independently by 357 Docker instance tags on jiayuanz3/swecontextbench and by 357 case files in cases/SWEContextBench Full/ at code rev 31bb0415.

endpoint_adjudication.question: Which Table 4 endpoint, if any, can this instrument resolve at its maximum available n of 357?
endpoint_adjudication.method: Ceiling taken as the published baseline-to-best-memory-arm gap; expected MemPhant effect = ceiling x measured packed recall@5 (0.7591); power by two-sided exact McNemar, alpha=0.05, scripts/instrument_power.py.

endpoints.verdict: NOT RESOLVABLE. The expected effect is below the MDE at every psi including 0.05. No tranche fixes this: 357 is the entire split.

endpoints.power_for_expected: 0.75 - 0.99 across the ENTIRE plausible psi range 0.15-0.40

endpoints.verdict: BORDERLINE. Resolvable only at low psi, and psi cannot be below the effect size itself, so this sits near its own floor. Worth recording as a diagnostic, not as a primary.
NO EFFECT TO MEASURE in the published data.

endpoint_adjudication.the_finding_that_changes_the_plan: The FAIL_TO_PASS-Tasks endpoint is powered at 0.75-0.99 across the WHOLE plausible psi range. That means a re-scoped stage 2 does not need a psi estimate at all -- the run is adequately powered whatever psi turns out to be. This voids the only preregistered purpose of the $40 stage 1 pilot.
endpoint_adjudication.a_trap_avoided: Table 4's FAIL_TO_PASS TESTS column moves 19.64 -> 55.95, roughly ten times the Resolved effect, and it is tempting to use it as the endpoint. It should NOT be used: tests are clustered within tasks (a correct patch passes all of a task's F2P tests at once), so the per-test n is not an independent n and the apparent effect size is inflated by within-task correlation. The per-TASK column (29.29 -> 40.40) is the honest version of the same signal, and it is the one costed above.

stage_1_adjudication.question: What decision does the $40 stage 1 pilot change?
stage_1_adjudication.preregistered_purpose: psi estimation for stage 2, plus live-defect discovery.

purpose_1_psi_estimation.why: Two independent reasons. (a) For the Resolved endpoint, stage 2 is cancelled, so sizing it is sizing a run that will not happen. (b) For the FAIL_TO_PASS-Tasks endpoint, power is 0.75-0.99 across the entire plausible psi range, so knowing psi does not change the go/no-go. Either way psi buys no decision.
purpose_1_psi_estimation.and_it_could_not_deliver_anyway: At n=30, expected discordant pairs are 4.5 (psi=0.15) to 9.0 (psi=0.30) and power for even the 11.11pp ceiling is 0.12. The pilot is below this programme's own n_d>=6 floor at the lower end. It was never going to be a measurement, which the brief already stated.

purpose_2_live_defect_discovery.why: No Claude Code scaffold exists in this repository. Pinning to Claude Code + Claude Sonnet 4.5 is mandatory for comparability to Table 3 and has never been round-tripped. This programme has had three adapters fail at first contact, two after money was authorised, and one that would have billed $211-634 for zero rows. That risk is real and unretired.
purpose_2_live_defect_discovery.but: It does not cost $40. The lock's own stage 0 acceptance item 5 already specifies the right instrument: drive the pinned scaffold end-to-end on ONE instance with a hard token cap, as a liveness probe and not a measurement. At Table 3's measured $0.67/task that is roughly $1, not $40.

recommendation.cancel: Stage 1 as scoped ($40, n=30). Its stated purpose is void and its unstated purpose is 40x overpriced.
recommendation.replace_with: A ~$1-$5 scaffold liveness probe: one to three Related instances, Claude Code + Claude Sonnet 4.5, hard token cap, official grader on the shipped gold patch (must resolve) and on an empty patch (must not resolve), plus one MemPhant-memory round trip proving the retrieved context reaches the agent. Decision it changes: whether a re-scoped stage 2 is executable at all. Nothing else can answer that, and it is the single largest unretired execution risk in the plan.
recommendation.then: Stage 2 re-scoped to FAIL_TO_PASS Tasks as primary is an OWNER decision, not a lane decision, because it changes what the headline claim is about. It is powered; Resolved is not. If the owner wants the Resolved headline specifically, the honest answer is that this instrument cannot supply it at any budget.
recommendation.spend_authorised_but_not_spent: Standing authority exists. It is not exercised here because no run below the re-scope decision changes a decision, except the ~$1 probe.

pattern_across_lanes: This is the third instrument in this programme to fail on a structural property rather than on MemPhant's quality, and the first to fail from the POWER side rather than the baseline side. S7 killed MDN browser-compat-data because a 20-line scoped_interval rule scores 1.0000 on every band; S6 found as-of saturation at 0.9064; both are cases where the gold is computable from the fact statements themselves, so a short rule saturates the baseline. SWE-ContextBench is the complement: its baseline is nowhere near saturated (19.68%), but the HEADROOM A MEMORY SYSTEM CAN ADDRESS is only 3.72pp, which is smaller than the instrument's own minimum detectable effect at its maximum n. Saturation kills an instrument from below; an effect ceiling under the MDE kills it from above. Both are properties of the instrument, both are cheap to check before spending, and neither is visible from a baseline rate alone.
